subject.title: feat: add Podman agent sandbox backend

question: Should native Podman be a bundled core sandbox backend, or should the existing sandbox plugin registry own the Podman-specific engine implementation?
rationale: Both approaches can be technically viable, but the repository policy favors plugin ownership for optional service/runtime integrations when the existing registry seam is sufficient; only maintainers can choose the permanent supported boundary.

options.title: Move Podman behind a plugin seam
options.body: Keep generic sandbox contracts in core and relocate Podman runtime, lifecycle, doctor, and documentation ownership to a dedicated plugin using the existing registry.

options.title: Approve bundled core ownership
options.body: Retain the current implementation only with explicit maintainer acceptance that Podman engine behavior and its security contract are a permanent core responsibility.

recommendation.title: Move Podman behind a plugin seam
recommendation.body: Keep generic sandbox contracts in core and relocate Podman runtime, lifecycle, doctor, and documentation ownership to a dedicated plugin using the existing registry.

likelyOwner.reason: The latest refactor establishes the core ownership shape that needs an explicit direction decision.
